population.text: Patients diagnosed with MPS VII aged 5 to 35 years; the 12 enrolled ranged in age from 8 to 25 years (median 14), 4 male and 8 female, 75% white, 50% Hispanic or Latino.

citations.quote: Study 301 was a phase 3 multicenter, randomized delayed start, study to assess the efficacy and safety of 4 mg/kg vestronidase alfa in patients diagnosed with MPS VII who were aged 5 to 35 years of age.

Of the 12 patients enrolled in the trial, 4 were male and 8 were female and ranged in age from 8 to 25 years (median 14 years). Nine patients were younger than 18 years of age. The majority of the patients were white (75%), with 50% of Hispanic or Latino ethnicity.

endpoint.text: For US regulatory purposes no pre-specified primary endpoint was declared; efficacy was based on the totality of the clinical data on a per-subject basis (with a Multi-Domain Responder Index and 6MWT among the endpoints). Percent reduction in urinary GAG (dermatan sulfate) was the EU primary and a US secondary endpoint.

citations.quote: As agreed upon with the Agency (see **Section 3.2**), study 301 did not have a pre-specified primary endpoint. Instead, efficacy would be determined based upon the totality of the evidence including the secondary and exploratory outcomes.
evaluation of the percent change in uGAGs was the primary efficacy endpoint in the EU and a secondary endpoint in the US.

n.text: N=12 (3 immediate MEPSEVII, 3 placebo 8 wk, 3 placebo 16 wk, 3 placebo 24 wk before crossover)

citations.quote: A total of 12 enrolled subjects were divided into four cohorts based upon placebo exposure of 0, 8, 16 or 24 weeks in duration prior to initiation of vestronidase alfa infusions. (Figure 7)

Three patients received MEPSEVII immediately for a duration of 48 weeks, 3 patients received placebo for 8 weeks then MEPSEVII for 40 weeks, 3 patients received placebo for 16 weeks then MEPSEVII for 32 weeks, and 3 patients received placebo for 24 weeks then MEPSEVII for 24 weeks.

result.text: After 24 weeks the LS mean difference in 6MWT between MEPSEVII and placebo was approximately 18 meters (SE 33); all patients were responders for uGAG (dermatan sulfate) with >=50% reduction, and urinary GAGs were maintained at approximately 60% to 80% reduction from baseline. The statistical team concluded no substantial evidence of efficacy; approval was based on the totality of evidence.

citations.quote: After 24 weeks of treatment, the least squares mean difference in 6MWT between vestronidase alpha and placebo periods is approximately 18 meters with a relatively large standard error of 33.
For this endpoint, a patient was identified as a “responder” if there was \ge 50\% reduction in uGAG (DS) excretion. All patients in Study 301 were identified as responders for this endpoint.
Subsequently, reductions in these urinary GAGs were maintained at approximately 60% to 80% from baseline.
The statistical review team concluded that no substantial evidence of efficacy is demonstrated in these data for 24 weeks of vestronidase alpha treatment in patients with MPS VII.

target_moa.text: Vestronidase alfa is a recombinant human beta-glucuronidase (rhGUS) enzyme replacement therapy identical in amino acid sequence to native human GUS; it carries mannose-6-phosphate residues that facilitate cell-surface receptor binding and internalization, and it reduces accumulated urinary glycosaminoglycans (GAGs) in patients with MPS VII who are deficient in beta-glucuronidase activity.

citations.quote: Vestronidase alfa is a recombinant human beta-glucuronidase (rhGUS) enzyme, purified from a genetically engineered stable Chinese hamster ovary (CHO) cell line and has the same amino acid sequence as the native human enzyme.

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (>=1 patient) were infusion site extravasation, diarrhea, rash, anaphylaxis, infusion site swelling, peripheral swelling, and pruritus. Anaphylaxis, the most serious risk, occurred in 2 of 20 patients in the clinical program.

citations.quote: Most common adverse reactions (≥1 patient) are: infusion site extravasation, diarrhea, rash, anaphylaxis, infusion site swelling, peripheral swelling and pruritus. (6.1)
Anaphylaxis to MEPSEVII was reported in 2 of 20 patients in the clinical program [see *Adverse Reactions (6.1)*].

detail.text: WARNING: ANAPHYLAXIS – Anaphylaxis has occurred with MEPSEVII administration, as early as the first dose; appropriate medical support should be readily available, patients closely observed during and for 60 minutes after infusion, and the infusion immediately discontinued if anaphylaxis occurs.

citations.quote: ## WARNING: ANAPHYLAXIS

- Anaphylaxis has occurred with MEPSEVII administration, as early as the first dose (5.1), therefore appropriate medical support should be readily available when MEPSEVII is administered.
- Closely observe patients during and for 60 minutes after MEPSEVII infusion (2.2, 5.1).
- Immediately discontinue the MEPSEVII infusion if the patient experiences anaphylaxis (2.2, 5.1).
